newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu inches down, money market rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu inches down, money market rates fall.

text.p: The leu opened weaker on Friday at 7,000/7500 to the dollar against about 6,900/7,000 at Thursday's close, when the greenback got support from some leu inflows on the money market, traders said.
Banks' quotes continued to reflect a wide range with leu-dollar rates from 6,000/100 to 7,150/7,500.

Dealers said short-term money market rates fell to some 300 percent from around 446 percent on Thursday as the market reacted to the fall to 226.31 percent from 426.5 percent in the average auctioned credit rate.
"I heard some operators might toss dollars on the market today and this probably could strengthen the leu a bit or help it stabilise at current levels," said one trader.
Leu-dollar retail rates firmed slightly, trading between 6,200/700 and 6,800/7,150 against Thursday's range of 6,500/7,500 to 7,000/8,000.
Operators said they were still waiting for the central bank to announce a new method to compute the reference exchange rates for the leu currency.
Two weeks ago the central bank said it would no longer compute the reference rate, which was a weighted average of operators' daily reports and was used for statistical and accounting purposes.
The latest reference rate of 7,744 lei to the dollar remained valid since then.
